images.title: Lowest floor is furthest down
images.purpose: Show that the lowest floor is the one furthest below the ground, so Floor −3 is lower than Floor −1.
images.composition: One tall vertical lift shaft centred on a white page, with a few evenly spaced floor lines and generous white space on both sides.
images.exact_structure: One vertical shaft of 6 equal floor levels, evenly spaced, listed top to bottom: +2, +1, 0 (ground, grey #6B7280 line), −1, −2, −3. A small teal #0072B2 lift box sits at floor −1. A reddish purple #CC79A7 box sits at floor −3, the lowest level. Exactly 6 floor lines, 2 coloured boxes.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The floor furthest below the ground is the lowest.
images.description: A lift shaft with floors +2 down to −3; the box at Floor −3 is highlighted as the lowest, with Floor −1 higher above it.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at Floor −1 and Floor −3 and say which one is further down.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
